subject: Performance profiling: synthetic traffic distribution & SLO correlation
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@rivertonhealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@rivertonhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask — benchmarking methodology details for RFP

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday. As part of our RFP we need a short, tight description of the performance benchmarking methodology Redwood would use to validate latency SLOs and throughput at scale for our clinical inference workload. Two quick asks: 1) a reproducible synthetic traffic profile (payload sizes, concurrency, sequence length distribution) we can run in our lab, and 2) a mapping that shows how measured metrics (p50/p95/p99, tail CPU/GPU utilization, queueing delay) correlate to the SLO tiers we care about.

We have strict windowing on processing (95% of requests <= 120ms p95) and a subset of long-context requests (max seq 4096) for batch jobs. Could you send a short plan and any sample artifacts we can run?

Best,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Riverton Health Systems — Platform Engineering
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@rivertonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — benchmarking methodology details for RFP

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a concise profiling plan and two runnable artifacts (synthetic-load-script.yaml and a CSV with sample expected outputs). High level summary below; the attachments include the exact wrk-compatible invocation and a small Python harness for sequence-length sampling.

Plan (summary):
- Traffic synthesis: mix of conversational (70% short: seq 64-256 tokens) and long-context batch (30% long: seq 1024-4096), payload composition driven by a configurable Zipf sampler (attachment: synthetic-load-script.yaml).
- Concurrency sweep: ramp 10 -> target RPS in steps, holding each step 5 minutes to warm KV cache and measure steady-state.
- Warmup & KV cache: run a 10-minute warmup with representative prefix traffic to populate remote KV caches and JIT caches; report cold vs warm latencies separately.
- Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, server-side queueing delay, GPU utilization, host CPU steal, token throughput, and memory/GPU tail usage.
- SLO correlation: we produce a mapping table (sample in CSV) that shows expected p95 vs RPS under batching and non-batching modes and identifies the operating RPS window that meets your 120ms p95 target for short-context mix.

Open questions for your QA team:
1) Do you plan to allow burst concurrency > baseline (e.g., occasional 3x bursts)?
2) Will the long-context workload be offline (scheduled batch) or mixed with interactive traffic?

I'll loop in Marissa for commercial framing and Ben for test harness details — Ben, can you confirm the script includes a flag for enabling/disabling quantized model variants and a boolean for forcing cold-start agents?

Cheers,
Dylan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — benchmarking methodology details for RFP

On Sep 1, 2026, at 10:04 AM, Dylan Brooks wrote:
> I'll loop in Marissa for commercial framing and Ben for test harness details — Ben, can you confirm the script includes a flag for enabling/disabling quantized model variants and a boolean for forcing cold-start agents?

Yes — the attached synthetic-load-script.yaml supports the following knobs:
- model_variant: full_fp16 | int8_quant | int4_quant
- cold_start: true|false (if true, kills and restarts an instance between runs to surface cold-start latency)
- batch_window_ms: [0, 10, 50] (to simulate batching thresholds)
- seq_dist_profile: conversational | longtail | custom (custom accepts a CSV distribution)

I added a small data collector that emits CSV rows per step with p50/p95/p99, median token latency, GPU utilization, and queue depth. The CSV filename in attachments is the output schema we used for the samples.

Ben
Senior Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@rivertonhealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@rivertonhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — benchmarking methodology details for RFP

Thanks — this is helpful and the knobs look comprehensive. A few clarifications from our QA lead:
- For the 120ms p95 target, can you provide a short table that says "expected max sustainable RPS" for the 70/30 mix under three operating modes: Dedicated (pinned 8xA100), Hosted burstable, and Private on our on-prem rack (NVIDIA H100 x4)?
- We need the scripts to avoid cloud-specific telemetry (we'll run in an air-gapped lab) — is the harness fully offline?
- For quantized variants, can you include a note on quality delta budgeting (we'll run evals but need a simple guidance number for RFP scorecards).

One more ask — can you mark warm vs cold runs clearly in the CSV output so we can plot separate histograms?

If you can get the table and annotated artifacts by COB tomorrow we'd appreciate it.

Regards,
Daniel
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@rivertonhealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T14:58:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — benchmarking methodology details for RFP

Hi Daniel —

Attached is a compact table and the annotated artifacts you requested. Highlights:
- Expected sustainable RPS (70/30 mix, short/long):
  * Dedicated (8xA100 pinned): ~410 RPS (p95 ~110ms, p99 ~240ms)
  * Hosted burstable (multi-tenant, autoscale): ~220 RPS (p95 ~115-130ms depending on burst profile)
  * Private on-prem (4xH100): ~360 RPS (p95 ~100-125ms depending on network fabric)

Notes and guidance:
- Warm vs cold: CSV includes a "run_mode" column with warm|cold; warm runs are taken after a 10-minute prefix warmup.
- Offline run: the harness is fully offline — no external telemetry, all logs written locally; instructions are first page of the YAML.
- Quality delta guidance for quantization: expect ~0.5-1.5% task-level metric degradation for int8 quant on typical chat-style tasks; int4 may reach 2-4% depending on prompt sensitivity. We recommend running your golden prompt set (we can provide an eval harness) to confirm.

Attachments: synthetic-load-script.yaml | redwood-latency-summary-20260902.csv | kpi-and-slo-definitions.pdf

Ben/Hannah, flag if any numbers need tuning before I send this back to Daniel.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@rivertonhealth.com>

Marissa —

This is exactly what we needed, thank you. The table lets us put sensible guardrails in the RFP scoring model. A couple quick follow-ups but otherwise we're good: 1) can Redwood share the small eval harness you mentioned (golden prompt runner) as a separate artifact? 2) we'll likely request a short on-site run for the final proof (tentative week of Oct 4).

Procurement will follow up on commercial terms.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Daniel
Riverton Health Systems
